title: Saltburn Cricket Club: 'Finger-clicking' cheating claim in Saltburn-Norton match investigated
description: An amateur cricket match has made global headlines after a fielder was accused of cheating by clicking his fingers to get a wicket.The North Yorkshire
body: An amateur cricket match has made global headlines after a fielder was accused of cheating by clicking his fingers to get a wicket.The North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League has started an investigation into a second XI Division 2 game between Saltburn and Norton.A viral video on social media appears to show a Saltburn fielder clicking his fingers as the ball passes Noman Shabir's bat before being caught by wicketkeeper Josh Bowes. Saltburn appeal and the umpire gives Shabir out.It has been suggested that the finger-clicking was designed to trick the umpire into thinking the batter edged the ball.Saltburn won by 159 runs and are top of Division 2 by 18 points."The league have received a formal complaint regarding alleged incidents in a Division Two game on Saturday," the league said in a statement on X."A full investigation has been initiated and until such time as the formal processes are complete no further comment will be made."Last week Bowes took eight catches in Saltburn's 22-run win over Shildon Railway. The men's Test record for catches by a keeper in an innings is seven.Bowes leads the league standings with 31 catches, 10 more than any other player.Rory Cotterill, who captained Middlesbrough second XI during a 29-run defeat by Saltburn last month, responded to a social media post containing the video and alleged two further incidents of cheating by Saltburn in that match.The original video of the incident has had more than five million views on X, with publications in Australia and New Zealand among those to report it.BBC Sport understands a meeting between Saltburn, the league and legal representatives is due to take place on Tuesday night. Norton declined to comment.

schema.headline: Saltburn Cricket Club: 'Finger-clicking' cheating claim in Saltburn-Norton match investigated

title: Amboseli elephant deaths:  Kenya Wildlife Service launches urgent inquiry after 14 carcasses found
description: An urgent investigation has been launched into the mysterious deaths of 14 elephants in southern Kenya near the Amboseli National Park.The Kenya Wildl
body: An urgent investigation has been launched into the mysterious deaths of 14 elephants in southern Kenya near the Amboseli National Park.The Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) told the BBC that experts were examining the carcasses and said that tissue samples had been sent to laboratories to determine whether the deaths were caused by disease, poisoning or another factor.The park and its surrounds are known as the Amboseli ecosystem, a vast area that straddles the border with Tanzania, which is famous for its wildlife.Officials say this is the first time in decades that elephant mortalities on this scale have been recorded in the region where they have successfully cracked down on poaching.KWS says there is currently no evidence pointing to a single cause of death.The carcasses include elephants of different ages and sexes, suggesting the deaths are not limited to a single family or demographic.The wildlife agency's head of communication, Duncan Wanyama, told local media the bodies had been found at different locations surrounding the Amboseli National Park, around 15km (nine miles) to 30km from its boundaries.According to figures from the Amboseli Trust for Elephants, which monitors the movements of the animals, there were more than 2,000 elephants in the Amboseli ecosystem as of 2025.

schema.headline: Amboseli elephant deaths:  Kenya Wildlife Service launches urgent inquiry after 14 carcasses found

title: Naga Munchetty swaps BBC One's Breakfast for Radio 5 Live Breakfast
description: Munchetty, 51, is among the best-paid presenters on the BBC's star salaries list, earning about £360,000 a year, according to the latest accounts.She
body: Munchetty, 51, is among the best-paid presenters on the BBC's star salaries list, earning about £360,000 a year, according to the latest accounts.She has interviewed major celebrities and politicians on the programme over the years ranging from Hillary Clinton and Michelle Obama to Sir Keir Starmer, Sir David Attenborough and Sir Rod Stewart.In 2016, she appeared on the BBC's Strictly Come Dancing.She has also been at the centre of some controversies during her time on BBC Breakfast.In 2019, she was initially found to have breached the BBC's guidelines over comments she made about a social media post from Donald Trump about four female politicians of colour.However, the BBC's director general then reversed that finding after deciding her words were not "sufficient to merit" upholding part of the complaint.In 2021, Munchetty and co-presenter Charlie Stayt were "spoken to and reminded of their responsibilities" after complaints about their reaction to a government minister's flag. Munchetty apologised for liking "offensive" tweets about the exchange.In June 2025, the Sun reported details of two alleged incidents which the paper said caused BBC bosses to speak to Munchetty about her conduct. That came amid reports of behind-the-scenes tensions on the show, and at the same time as the programme's editor Richard Frediani took extended leave following allegations about his behaviour.Frediani returned to work two weeks later and remains editor of BBC Breakfast.At the time, the BBC said it did not comment on individual cases but took all complaints about conduct at work extremely seriously. Munchetty and Frediani did not comment on the reports.The programme won a Bafta TV Award last year for best news coverage for a special about the Post Office scandal.

schema.headline: Naga Munchetty swaps BBC One's Breakfast for Radio 5 Live Breakfast

title: Commonwealth Games 2026: Gymnast Ruby Evans wins first gold for Wales
description: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Ruby Evans is a world silver medallist in the women's floorGymnast Ruby Evans has won Wales' first Commonweal
body: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Ruby Evans is a world silver medallist in the women's floorGymnast Ruby Evans has won Wales' first Commonwealth Games gold in Glasgow with victory in the floor final.The 19-year-old performed well in the final routine of the women's programme, with silver for England's Abigail Martin, whose team-mate Shantae-Eve Amankwaah took bronze.Evans left the arena in tears on Sunday after her disappointing sixth in the all-around individual competition, coming after Wales finished fourth in the team event.Now, after Welsh identical twins Abigail and Emily Roper won bronze medals within a couple of hours of each other on Monday, Evans has delivered gold. It was the first victory for Team Wales in Scotland and a ninth medal alongside two silver and six bronze.There is also a guaranteed podium position for boxer Connor Williams after he reached the semi-finals.How anger drove Evans to golden momentEvans created history by winning Wales' first women's artistic gymnastics Commonwealth Games gold."I couldn't be happier," she said."I couldn't have done any more on that floor and I knew whatever the result was after, I couldn't have done any better. I'm just happy that it is a gold."Evans admitted she had been almost angry when she went out to compete after the disappointment of earlier performances in Glasgow."The first day we came here, I did really well and I got through to the all-around final," said the Cardiff teenager."That didn't go to plan and it was a very silly mistake, so I was really angry with that. "So I knew when I came out here I needed to do something for my country and that was the floor routine."Figure caption, Ruby Evans wins Wales' first gold of Commonwealth GamesThe Welsh national anthem was played for the first time in Glasgow during these Games with Evans at the top of the podium."I was really excited to hear the national anthem," said Evans."When something like that plays in your brain, you think 'my god I'd love that to happen'."To see the dragon on the flag, I was so excited because I am so passionately Welsh."Evans outlined how she would celebrate before she leaves Glasgow tomorrow.She said: "I will be seeing family, maybe go for some food. There's tenpin bowling in Team Wales house. I think they want to do all that."

schema.headline: Commonwealth Games 2026: Gymnast Ruby Evans wins first gold for Wales

title: Xabi Alonso's first Chelsea match was a tale of four strikers
description: Xabi Alonso's first match as Chelsea manager was defined by four strikers - an untouchable one, one that struggled again and could leave, a promising
body: Xabi Alonso's first match as Chelsea manager was defined by four strikers - an untouchable one, one that struggled again and could leave, a promising talent, and one that could join.The star was Joao Pedro, who scored a nine-minute hat-trick to help Alonso's side to a 6-4 win against Western Sydney Wanderers in a match that highlighted the gulf between Premier League and A-League teams.Perhaps it was the disappointment of being left out of Brazil's World Cup squad that inspired the forward to showcase his finishing prowess as well as his power and pace in an entertaining spectacle at Accor Stadium.Alonso described Joao Pedro as "very, very hungry" and "determined to have a great season".For the most part however it was a sloppy and imperfect performance by Chelsea, with the Blues still adjusting to the effects of jet lag.There were few other standouts other than Joao Pedro, but Dastan Satpaev was one.The 17-year-old scored the first goal of Alonso's reign - and in spectacular fashion - after just six minutes.Strangely, the Kazakhstan forward did so as a triallist - because he cannot formally complete his move from FC Kairat to Stamford Bridge until 12 August.By contrast, his fellow starting forward Liam Delap again struggled, as he has in almost every appearance for Chelsea since his £30m move from Ipswich last summer.Delap appears short of confidence and could now be sold, with Chelsea advancing talks to sign Danny Welbeck, 35, as an experienced replacement.Welbeck has agreed personal terms and there is optimism at Chelsea that a deal can be reached, although his club Brighton are refusing to comment.Chelsea are also in talks to sign midfielder Jordan Henderson, 36, from Brentford as they look to add experience and leadership to their squad after a disappointing 2025-26 season.When asked about signing the two older players, Alonso replied: "We need balance, to have a complete squad and make a good team. For that, we have an idea and plan." Beyond the narratives surrounding strikers, with injured Emmanuel Emegha and Nicolas Jackson also on the books, it was only a very early glimpse of what to expect from Alonso's Chelsea.Satpaev is attempting to become the first Kazakh player to appear in a Premier League match. In his homeland, he is a superstar. He has already played for his national team and attracted fans from his home country to both the open training session on Sunday and the match on Tuesday in Sydney. Quick, sharp in the box and relatively small in stature, Satpaev is stylistically often compared to former Argentina and Manchester City striker Sergio Aguero. Asked whether he will get a chance at Chelsea this season amid talk of a potential loan move, Alonso said: "We still have to take decisions."I knew Dastan from Almaty," added Alonso, who faced the player with his former club Real Madrid last season. "He is a ball threat, he attacks the inner channel well and is good as a striker coming from the outside. "He is really strong, really quick and I have been really impressed with him."The former Liverpool midfielder, who was a vocal presence on the touchline, used the 4-2-3-1 system favoured by Enzo Maresca, who was Chelsea head coach this time last year.With players still on holiday after the World Cup - including club record £117m signing Morgan Rogers - several youngsters were given an opportunity. Midfield trio Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli, Reggie Walsh and Reggie Watson all impressed, with the latter the only player to play the full game.Nicoll-Jazuli and Watson, both 16, anchored the midfield together for long periods, while 17-year-old Walsh impressed in a more advanced role.In his pre-match media conference, Alonso expressed surprise at how well the seven academy players drafted in to fill gaps in the squad had performed in training. Landon Emenalo, 18, has also been given a significant opportunity, with no other left-backs available.The only senior player other then Joao Pedro to particularly impress was winger Jamie Gittens, who made it three goals in three appearances in pre-season, following his two in behind-closed-doors friendlies against EFL opposition.

schema.headline: Xabi Alonso's first Chelsea match was a tale of four strikers

title: Schools to offer technical subjects to pupils from age 14, Burnham says
description: Secondary school pupils in England will be able to study subjects like manufacturing and AI in addition to core academic learning under reforms outlin
body: Secondary school pupils in England will be able to study subjects like manufacturing and AI in addition to core academic learning under reforms outlined by Prime Minister Andy Burnham.The government said the courses, which would be available from Year 10, would be linked to local industries and designed to give children a clearer pathway into work.Data published this year showed more than one million young people across the UK were not in education, employment or training, the highest level in more than 12 years.Few details have been published about how the new vocational courses would work in practice and it is not clear how they would operate in areas with low industrial activity.The BBC understands that the government expects the new pathways into work to be up and running in some areas by 2028.Later on Tuesday, the government also announced a new bursary of up to £4,500 for some families who would lose out on money if their children wanted to do an apprenticeship, because the child benefit they would lose out on would be worth more than the apprenticeship starter salary.Speaking at a train manufacturing site in Derby, Burnham said: "We've had a system built for too long around the university route and it sends a message to some young people that they're some kind of second-class citizens, and it's just not right."They need an education system that works for them as well, that offers a path to all young people, that's balanced between academic and technical."The prime minister said he was "on a mission" to reduce the number of young people not in education, employment or training - known as "Neet" - but declined to put a target date on his ambition."The trend is rising at the moment, so the first thing I've got to do is to stop that rise," he said."It's hard to put a firm date on the moment when you can say there are fewer than now."However, shadow work and pensions secretary Helen Whately said while there was a "broad consensus" on improving vocational education, it was "not a big bold announcement".She told BBC Breakfast: "What's going on there is a drastic shortage of jobs because Labour's policies over the last couple of years have killed job opportunities for young people. This announcement will not solve that."Under the proposals, pupils would continue to study core maths, English and science but would also have the option of combining the subjects with technical education.It will include the chance to gain work experience and create connections with local employers, Burnham said, with the government saying the policy will eventually drive down the amount spent on welfare for young people.While some business leaders welcomed the move, others said youth jobs could be boosted by other means.Jon White, chief financial officer at building materials firm Huws Gray, said employers were "struggling" with a lack of incentives to hire younger people, pointing to the government narrowing the gap between the national minimum wage for under-21s and the national living wage.He also said the government should change the rules around how employers can spend the apprenticeship levy. The levy is paid by big employers, with the money raised available to all businesses to help fund apprenticeship training - but White said businesses should be allowed to use it to pay young people's wages as well.For schools, the Association of School and College Leaders said they welcomed the prime minister's ambition, but warned that schools could face capacity issues as they continued to face tight budgets and implemented radical reforms to special education needs.The National Education Union said the new proposals would "hit the skids unless there is sufficient investment in schools", while the NAHT school leaders' union called for "greater clarity" about funding and practical details.Along with the changes to learning, Ofsted will change the way it measures performance and will inspect for technical education, but it is not clear how this will fit alongside national measures designed to hold schools to account.Tuesday's announcement is the latest in a series of policies in recent years designed to offer a vocational route in education as a counter-balance to high numbers of young people going to university. Former prime minister Sir Keir Starmer previously said a technical education should be valued as much as a university degree, scrapping Labour's previous ambition to get half of children to university.In 2020, T-levels were introduced as a technical education alternative to A-Levels in England, with courses including construction, agriculture and health.Starmer announced earlier this year that V-levels would be an additional vocational option for students post-16 from 2027.Where T-levels are a set course broadly equivalent to three A-levels, V-levels would be equivalent to one A-level, allowing students to mix and match academic and vocational subjects.The changes announced on Tuesday will only impact England, but improving access to technical and vocational education has been a common focus for governments in Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland too in recent years.The policy will build on local initiatives like the MBacc, or Greater Manchester Baccalaureate, which was launched in September 2024 by Burnham when he was the city's mayor.It has provided a framework for pupils to pick GCSE subjects in both academic and technical subjects which align with growing local industries, like green energy or digital.Teenagers under this programme have also been promised more careers advice and work experience that links to seven sectors of work.Education Secretary Lucy Powell said the announcement marked the "start of a real shared effort with employers, businesses, mayors and councils to design an education system that connects young people to jobs and careers in their local area".In May, an interim report by former Alan Milburn warned the number of young people not in employment, education or training risked leading to a "lost generation".That report was published the same day as figures from the Office for National Statistics showed more than one in eight of UK 16- to 24-year-olds were Neet at the start of this year.Milburn told the BBC the announcement on education would help prevent children becoming Neet by "equipping them with the skills and aptitudes that they're going to need to be successful in the future labour market".Liberal Democrat education spokesperson Munira Wilson said there had to be provisions to allow pupils flexibility to "change direction and move between 'academic' and 'technical'"."We must not allow these changes to predetermine children's futures at just 14, baking in disadvantage," she added.

schema.headline: Schools to offer technical subjects to pupils from age 14, Burnham says

title: House of the Dragon star Bethany Antonia joins Strictly Come Dancing 2026 line-up
description: House of the Dragon star Bethany Antonia is the latest celebrity to join this year's line-up for Strictly Come Dancing.Antonia has portrayed dragon-ri
body: House of the Dragon star Bethany Antonia is the latest celebrity to join this year's line-up for Strictly Come Dancing.Antonia has portrayed dragon-rider Lady Baela Targaryen in HBO's Game of Thrones prequel since 2022. She is currently starring as Eurydice in the Tony Award-winning musical Hadestown in London's West End.The singer and actress has also appeared in series including Nolly, Stay Close, Stath Lets Flats, and Doctor Who.In a statement, Antonia said: "I can't quite believe that I will be heading to the Strictly ballroom this September! I have grown up watching Strictly, and I am so excited to take the challenge on and (hopefully!) learn a new skill. See you on the dancefloor!"She is the ninth celebrity to be confirmed for this year's series, joining stars including  Delta Goodrem, Lacey Turner, Dani Dyer and Jaime Winstone.More celebrities are set to be announced in the coming weeks, with 15 expected in the final line-up.Scroll down to see the rest of this year's line-up so far:Jaime Winstone launched her acting career in 2004 and her film credits include Bullet Boy, Tomb Raider and Wild Bill, as well stage productions such as 2:22 A Ghost Story.The actress, who also won acclaim for her portrayal of Barbara Windsor in the BBC biopic Babs, said she was "so excited" to be joining the dance competition. The actress said in a statement she was "no stranger to a dance floor", but added that ballroom is "a whole new world for me"."I love a challenge though," she continued, "so can't wait to enter my showgirl era and get super sparkly!"Winstone has also appeared in TV series such as Poirot, Dead Set, Torvill & Dean, Mad Dogs, Count Abdulla and Four Lives.After playing Windsor in Babs, Winstone stepped into the late actress's famous role of Peggy Mitchell in EastEnders, appearing in flashback specials, most recently in the soap's 40th anniversary last year. Celebrity hair stylist Chris Appleton is also part of this year's line-up.Appleton, best known for his work with Kim Kardashian, joins singer-songwriter Delta Goodrem, EastEnders actress Lacey Turner and reality star Dani Dyer in the battle for the Glitterball trophy.The Leicester-born Color Wow creative director said: "I'm thrilled to be joining Strictly Come Dancing and coming home to the UK for this incredible experience."He has also created red carpet looks for the likes of Jennifer Lopez, Katy Perry and Ariana Grande, while having his work showcased on the covers of publications including Vogue, Harper's Bazaar and Vanity Fair."I've always believed that the best things happen when you take a chance and try something new," added the 43-year-old, who this year released a memoir entitled Your Roots Don't Define You."I may know my way around a salon floor, but the dance floor is a whole different story - and I can't wait to get started."Josh Widdicombe, Emma Willis and Johannes Radebe will take over as Strictly presenters this year, following the departures of Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman.The first line-up announcements were made significantly earlier than usual - the BBC usually confirms the line-up in August.  Speaking to ITV's Good Morning Britain in June, Ballas said: "There are going to be some people on there that will make you go 'wow'."Asked about the new presenting trio, Ballas said she was "very excited to see what they bring" to the show. "I know they took lots of chemistry tests, as did everybody, and those chemistry tests have brought those three people together, and I believe it's absolutely unbelievable," she said.Ballas described the number of new elements on this year's show as "quite extraordinary", but added that it will still feel familiar to viewers."I don't think they'll change the show too much, maybe tweaks here and there, but no major changes."Ballas, Craig Revel Horwood, Motsi Mabuse and Anton Du Beke will all return as judges.Regular pro dancers including Amy Dowden, Dianne Buswell, Katya Jones, Vito Coppola and Aljaz Skorjanec will all be back on the dance floor.However, professional dancers Gorka Marquez, Nadiya Bychkova, Luba Mushtuk, Karen Hauer and Michelle Tsiakkas will not be returning this year.

schema.headline: House of the Dragon star Bethany Antonia joins Strictly Come Dancing 2026 line-up

title: Powell says student loan system at top of her in-tray
description: Lucy Powell has said she wants to make sure the student loans system is "fair" and that the issue is at the top of her in-tray as the new education se
body: Lucy Powell has said she wants to make sure the student loans system is "fair" and that the issue is at the top of her in-tray as the new education secretary.Labour's deputy leader told the BBC she stood by comments she made in February that the interest rates graduates with Plan 2 loans were paying were "egregious".She said she was committed to looking at the issue, although acknowledged she "can't make any promises" about changes.Plan 2 loans were taken out by students in England between September 2012 and July 2023, and are still issued in Wales. Graduates pay back what they earn above the repayment threshold at a rate of 9%.In November last year, then-Chancellor Rachel Reeves said the repayment threshold for students with Plan 2 loans would be frozen at £29,385 between 2027 and 2030, instead of rising with inflation.The change would result in students starting to repay their loans sooner than they would otherwise have done, and their rising salaries leading to greater repayments.Campaigners have called for that decision to be reversed.Reeves later said the government's measures were "fair and proportionate" for getting "the balance right between tax and spending".In April, the government said interest on some student loans in England - including Plan 2 - would be capped at 6%.Speaking to Matt Chorley on BBC Radio 5 Live, Powell said she was "very familiar" with the issue as her eldest child has a Plan 2 loan.She said: "I think it's not just about the threshold of when people start to pay it back, but also the interest rate which is RPI [retail prices index] plus 3%."I think I've called it in the past egregious and I'm not going to change my opinion on that just because I'm now the secretary of state."The government has committed to a review of that, it's very much at the top of my in-tray as the secretary of state, and I want to make sure we look at this so it's fair for students."Powell described it as a "real cost-of-living issue" for young people, adding: "They're paying high repayments and never, ever paying off the capital of their student loan."Pressed on whether it is something she will look at, Powell replied: "Yes. I can't make any promises, but it needs looking at."MPs on the Treasury Committee this month said comparing student loan repayments to phone contracts or cinema tickets "amounted to mis-selling" by government.It came after a BBC investigation found the government compared student loan repayments to £30-a-month phone contracts in promotional presentations to teenagers a decade ago.Earlier this year, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said she would cut the rate of interest charged on Plan 2 loans, capping it at RPI only. The current RPI rate is 3%.

schema.headline: Powell says student loan system at top of her in-tray

title: Can Burnham's vision for Manchester's schools work for the rest of England?
description: Two years ago, I stood at the back of a conference room in Manchester Hall, sipping a coffee and watching Andy Burnham unveil his vision for transform
body: Two years ago, I stood at the back of a conference room in Manchester Hall, sipping a coffee and watching Andy Burnham unveil his vision for transforming technical education in Greater Manchester.He had announced plans for the Manchester Baccalaureate, or MBacc, the year before, and, armed with PowerPoint slides and guest speakers, was running through the ins and outs in front of a room full of education and business leaders.Now, as prime minister, Burnham has announced plans to make that idea national, and overhaul the technical education system across the whole of England.The details are still scarce at this stage. We know it will involve giving pupils the option to study more vocational courses and take up work experience from Year 10, but how it will work in practice is still up in the air.One thing that is certain is that the thinking behind it, and the ambition, is the same as that which underpins the MBacc: a determination to give teenagers a clear, step-by-step route into more practical and technical jobs.The trouble is, the MBacc itself can be quite a difficult concept to get your head around if you're not familiar with it.Let's be clear from the start: it's not another type of qualification, like the T-levels and V-levels announced in England in recent years.Instead, it's a framework that aims to give teenagers a "clear line of sight to good jobs" in vocational and technical areas.The best way to think about it is a step-by-step route - picture a flow chart - that teenagers can follow from school into any given technical career. It's set up in parallel to a more clearly defined academic route. During that conference event in July 2024, Burnham and other speakers made clear that those who want to go on to desk jobs can follow a well-trodden path of GCSEs, A-levels, and a university degree.But for those who want more practical careers, the landscape is much more complicated. The MBacc is best seen as an effort to simplify that landscape, spelling out for teenagers who want to go into more vocational or technical careers which courses they can study, and ensuring they have the opportunity to study them along with hands-on work experience.It spells out routes to careers in seven different categories:Construction and the green economyCreative, culture and sportDigital and technologyEducation and early yearsFinancial, business and professional servicesHealth and social careManufacturing and engineeringIts success is difficult to measure, since the MBacc is still in its infancy. It's not until 2030 that it seeks to achieve its mission of guaranteeing every young person a clear path to good jobs. By 2035, the aim is for every young person to have 45 days of work experience by the time they're 19.According to the most recent data, the MBacc has been rolled out across 101 secondary schools and colleges in Greater Manchester - about 40% of the total. The Greater Manchester Combined Authority says 1,405 young people accessed workplace experiences during its second year.Time will tell, as those teenagers leave school and enter the world of work, how transformative it will be.And what works in Greater Manchester may not work everywhere else. The prime minister has stated explicitly that he wants to expand the approach across England. "I created the Greater Manchester Baccalaureate or MBacc... to bridge the gap between our schools and our employers," he wrote in the Times. "Now we're taking that idea national."It may well be scalable. The seven MBacc "gateways" - although designed specifically around Greater Manchester's "fastest-growing industries" - are actually quite broad-ranging. They mirror some of the areas already targeted by efforts to boost technical education at a national level. There are T-levels in construction areas as well as in education and early years, for example.But there will be challenges along the way. The prime minister is clear that he wants technical and vocational education to be tied to local economies. He plans to work with local leaders, employers and schools, to "identify the industries driving growth in local areas and make sure that local kids have a clear route into them".If that's to be the case, he will need to make sure that teenagers in all parts of England - including in areas without thriving industries - don't fall through the gaps.

schema.headline: Can Burnham's vision for Manchester's schools work for the rest of England?

title: Wildfires in south-west France flare up as region braces for new 40C heatwave
description: This summer's fourth heatwave was expected to start by Wednesday, bringing temperatures in the area to 40C.Similar temperatures are expected in Spain.
body: This summer's fourth heatwave was expected to start by Wednesday, bringing temperatures in the area to 40C.Similar temperatures are expected in Spain.Dozens of communities are still threatened by wildfires that forced more than 70,000 to evacuate their homes over the last week - although many have now been allowed back.The Madrid region has been especially affected, but Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said while there were highly challenging hours and days ahead, light was beginning to appear "at the end of the tunnel".In neighbouring Portugal, 400 firefighters were tackling a large fire on three active fronts in the eastern Guarda area.The French city of Bordeaux, which has a population of 260,000, is not currently under threat, according to officials, despite the fact that one of the wildfires burning on Monday came only 15km (9 miles) from the city's periphery. But Commander Rémi Lassoureille, who is leading the firefighting response in the Gironde region, is still worried about the western edge of the wildfire."We are frightened about the impact on Bordeaux and the metropolitan area," he said. Air quality in the city also deteriorated greatly."By Sunday evening everything had really begun to empty out," a holidaymaker from Essex told the BBC, adding that the air was "really smoky" with bits of ash. "People were staying indoors, so it was eerie, and very sad."The majority of residents and tourists were wearing masks and the smell of smoke clung on to clothes for days, she said. A firefighter "got a round of applause" as he walked through the Marché des Chartrons in Bordeaux where restaurants were having to close their doors because of the ash in the air, she added."The city has been very quiet," said Graham White, president of the Bordeaux British Community. "The shops, restaurants and cafes are fairly empty... Interestingly on Sunday when there was still smoke, there were people brave enough to sit outside on terraces."White, who has been living in the area for several years, said this sort of event was "something significant". But some news reports had suggested the situation in Bordeaux was "akin to being the next Great Fire of London", which was not the case, White added.Health Minister Stéphanie Rist said the government was being "very vigilant" in terms of air pollution and urged people in the affected areas to stay indoors. Peggy Plouhinec, the general director of Château Picque Caillou - one of the few wine estates on the west side of Bordeaux - told the BBC that her business chose to close at the weekend because of the smoke, but that the situation had improved since then and that a bout of rain on Sunday night had helped. While her vineyards were not at risk, she said tourists had "deserted" the region. "The hospitality sector will be impacted this summer, that's for sure," she added. "What is happening is unprecedented. We're lucky that we haven't been too affected yet, but the business will still suffer from the lower numbers of tourists.""But many people have lost their homes or their businesses, not to mention the firefighters who have been hard at work for weeks now and who must be exhausted."One resident of Cap Ferret, which was evacuated late last week, told French media that his main concern now was for the peninsula he lived in, rather than the big city city inland."Everyone talks about saving Bordeaux, but in Bordeaux there's nothing but concrete. Have you ever seen concrete burn?""Here, there are only trees... and when you see all that has burned, it's a catastrophe."Additional reporting by Xavier Pallas

title: Laughter and tears at Dame Penelope Keith funeral in Guildford
description: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Dame Penelope Keith (pictured in 1980) was an actressByZac Sherratt and Joshua AskewSouth EastUpdated 5 hours
body: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Dame Penelope Keith (pictured in 1980) was an actressByZac Sherratt and Joshua AskewSouth EastUpdated 5 hours agoDame Penelope Keith's funeral has been hailed as "wonderful, beautiful and absolutely amazing" by her friends.The actress, who starred in The Good Life and To The Manor Born, "died peacefully whilst living with cancer at her home" on 29 June at the age of 86.Crowds lined the streets to say their goodbyes to the "very special lady" as her coffin travelled through her home town of Milford in Surrey before the service at Guildford Cathedral.Broadcaster, writer and former politician Gyles Brandreth said the funeral was "filled with a mixture of sadness but laughter and gratitude as well because we were celebrating a great actress"."It was a wonderful way to remember a remarkable person," he told BBC Radio Surrey.Posting on X later, he said: "There was laughter and tears at Guildford Cathedral this morning - a truly beautiful and deeply moving funeral service for Dame Penelope Keith - what a lady and what a perfect service."It caught her completely. She was very special."Image caption, Many people gathered to pay their respects to the late actressBrandreth described Dame Penelope as one of the nicest and kindest people. "Her love of Surrey was in everything she did," he said. "Her sense of community... belonging and working for the community was considerable."Image caption, Dame Penelope was described as "great fun"Sarah Cliff told BBC Radio Surrey Dame Penelope had been part of her childhood. "[She] was known to me as Auntie Penny", said Cliff. "She was great fun". Cliff, the daughter of the acting couple Michael Robbins and Hal Dyer, added that the service was "beautiful". "I've never been to this cathedral. It's airy, it's light, it's lovely," she said. Image caption, Sarah Cliff (pictured) is the daughter of actors Michael Robbins and Hal DyerDoreen Walford said she and the late actress went back a long way. She told BBC Radio Surrey the pair used to live close by and they had worked together. "Everybody could talk to her," she said.On seeing the procession, she added: "I am so glad I came. It was absolutely amazing." Follow BBC Surrey on Facebook, external, X, external, and Instagram, external and listen to BBC Radio Surrey on Sounds. title: Odyssey translator slams Nolan's film adaptation as 'gimmicky' with 'no sex'
description: Odyssey translator writes scathing review of Nolan film adaptationImage source, Universal PicturesByEmma SaundersCulture reporterUpdated 5 hours agoSi
body: Odyssey translator writes scathing review of Nolan film adaptationImage source, Universal PicturesByEmma SaundersCulture reporterUpdated 5 hours agoSir Christopher Nolan's latest film, The Odyssey, may have won rave reviews from critics and done storming business at the box office - but one person is definitely not happy.Emily Wilson, the academic whose 2017 translation of Homer's Odyssey was cited by the director as an influence on his adaptation of the poem, has written a scathing review of the movie.Published in the London Review of Books, external, Wilson said she "would be ashamed to have written any of this script", describing the film's narrative structure as "gimmicky.""The writing is abysmal," she said. "None of the characters has convincing motivation for their actions or words. There are no sex scenes, and all the food looks horrible."Image source, Universal PicturesImage caption, Lupita Nyong'o stars as Helen of Troy in Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey"It lacks psychological, emotional, political and ethical depth," Wilson wrote, while also acknowledging that Sir Christopher's work had sparked renewed interest in Homer's classic."The release of The Odyssey is still an event to celebrate," Wilson noted. "This epic is bringing audiences back to cinemas... translations of Odyssey, including mine, are flying off the shelves... [and] perhaps the film will persuade a few college administrators not to cut their literature, language and history departments."Nolan... is doing his best to get the general public reading again, and I am grateful."Image source, Universal PicturesImage caption, The Odyssey is Sir Christopher Nolan's first film since the Oscar-winning OppenheimerBut she was left largely disappointed by the three-hour epic"I had hoped that Nolan's affinity with these Homeric themes might push him to new creative heights, and enable him to conjure more believable characters," she wrote."But The Odyssey features his usual combination of grandiosity and superficiality... the film's vision is too confused, its characters too underdeveloped, to deliver what it half-promises in terms of big ideas – although it is very good at conveying big bangs and big giants."Wilson added that her teenagers had "had a good time" seeing the blockbuster at the cinema."It's a family-friendly audiovisual spectacle, like an elaborate Fourth of July fireworks display - and with about the same level of narrative and emotional depth," she said."There are more female characters than in most Nolan movies, thanks to the source material. But none of them has much to say, in contrast to the characterisations in the poem."During his press tour for the film, Sir Christopher told Empire magazine, external that he used the opening line of Wilson's translation ("Tell me about a complicated man") as a guide for his Odysseus, played by Matt Damon.Image source, Universal PicturesImage caption, Anne Hathaway plays Odysseus's wife Penelope, who's also mother to their son Telemachus (Tom Holland)In contrast to Wilson's take, the latest adaptation has received rapturous reviews from film critics.It is the director's first movie since 2023's Oppenheimer, which won the Academy Award for best picture.The Telegraph declared The Odyssey the "film of the year", while Metro added that the movie would "change cinema forever".The Times described it as "a masterpiece in every way", and the Standard praised the film as a "colossal piece of cinema".The Odyssey, which was released earlier this month, stars Zendaya, Tom Holland, Robert Pattinson, Anne Hathaway, Charlize Theron alongside Nyong'o and Damon.It follows Odysseus (Damon), the Greek king of Ithaca, on his long and perilous journey home from the Trojan War to return to his wife and son (Hathaway and Holland).

title: French Navy carries out 'shooting drill' in English Channel mid BBC interview
description: Figure caption, A French Navy boat was heard firing shots during a BBC interview earlierByDaniel SextonSouth EastUpdated 4 hours agoA French Navy patr
body: Figure caption, A French Navy boat was heard firing shots during a BBC interview earlierByDaniel SextonSouth EastUpdated 4 hours agoA French Navy patrol boat appeared to fire a round of gunshots "without warning" in the English Channel during a BBC interview with the UK shadow home secretary.Conservative MP Chris Philp was being interviewed about small boat crossings by BBC journalist Michael Keohan as a French warship passed by at 09:15 BST (10:15 CET), about three miles from the French coast.Keohan said there were 17 shots but "no warnings" from the boat about 300m away, which left Philp believing it was an intimidation tactic to "stop us covering migrant crossings".The French authorities said it was part of a training exercise, unrelated to the presence of a British ship, which it said was out of range of fire.Philp dismissed this claim as "not credible", adding: "There were no warnings in place about live firing training exercises."It looked and sounded exactly like deliberate intimidation."Image source, BBC/Jack ValpyImage caption, Chris Philp MP, the Shadow Home Secretary, said it felt like an intimidation tactic or warning shotsThe captain of the fishing boat which hosted the interview, Matt Coker, said he had "never seen anything like it before".The French authorities said the boat, PSP Flamant, was not engaged in an operation to monitor migrant boats.Keohan said there were 17 shots, adding: "There was no warning for our boat, no signs given that this was the French's intention."Philp said it "felt to me like an attempted intimidation to stop us covering migrant crossings".Image source, Richard Pohle/The TimesImage caption, A French patrol officer at the back of the boat was seen pointing a pistol towards the seaAt sea, Keohan described it as "the most unusual moment... in the quiet of the Channel" when the gunshots rang out mid-interview.A French patrol officer at the back of the boat was seen pointing a pistol towards the sea. It is believed that is where the shots came from.Keohan, who was on board the vessel with a reporter from The Times, added: "There was no warning for our boat, no signs given, that this was the French's intention. "Even now it's still not clear what the patrol boat was aiming at."Image source, Chris Philp MPImage caption, The MP was being interviewed by the BBC at the time of the incidentAfter the incident, Philp said: "It is extraordinary that the French Navy will fire live rounds to defend their waters against a visiting British politician but cannot bear to do anything about stopping illegal Channel crossings."If France showed people smugglers half the seriousness they showed me, the boats would stop. "Instead, the French wave them through and pass them off to the British coastguard so it's our problem."He said he would be raising the issue with the French ambassador.'Normal activity'A UK government spokesperson said: "This is a matter for the French authorities."The French authorities said a handgun shooting exercise had taken place by the public service patrol boat Flamant off the coast of Cap de Gris-Nez.A spokesperson said: "In order to maintain their high level of operability in the current international context, the units of the French Navy train regularly."Individual training of the combatant is part of the normal activity of a ship in operations."The regulatory signals as provided for by international standards for this shooting exercise were displayed, and the safety gauge was respected."This exercise is unrelated to the presence of a British ship in the area, which was out of range of fire."The PSP Flamant was not engaged in an operation to monitor migrant boats."Earlier this month, a Russian warship, shadowed by a Royal Navy vessel, carried out a live-fire artillery exercise just 46 miles (74km) south of Plymouth.Follow BBC Kent on Facebook, external, on X, external, on Instagram, external and listen to BBC Radio Kent on Sounds. title: Zinedine Zidane waited for France - now what will he bring to role?
description: In September, the France national team will have a new face on the touchline for the first time in 14 years.By the time the appointment was announced
body: In September, the France national team will have a new face on the touchline for the first time in 14 years.By the time the appointment was announced on Tuesday morning, it had long been an open secret that Zinedine Zidane would succeed Didier Deschamps this summer.Talks between the former Real Madrid manager and the French football authorities kicked off as early as February 2025 - after Zidane's former team-mate Deschamps announced a few weeks earlier he would step down following the 2026 World Cup.At his unveiling in Paris, Zidane was keen to highlight the time he had spent waiting on the sidelines and preparing for the job."I had several offers in the last four or five years, but I turned them all down," an emotional Zidane said. "The national team is the only thing I wanted."While his enthusiasm at taking the job was the overarching theme of Tuesday morning's news conference in the French capital, the midfield legend offered few clues to France fans as to how he would approach the role.Even a question on Kylian Mbappe's captaincy was bypassed: "The most important thing for him now is to rest, we'll have the chance to speak in September."When asked about his preferred style of play, Zidane opted against going into tactical detail."I can't explain to you in just a couple of words how we're going win. I have to arrive, meet with the players, and explain my plans to them. After that, it'll be up to me to keep this team winning."However, Zidane confirmed his intention "to do things differently".He went on to signal that there would be a degree of "continuation" from the work of his predecessor, which he made sure to praise."I'm going to try do what I know how to, but it won't be a complete break either."So what will Zidane bring to the French dugout?Zidane and Deschamps, two 1998 World Cup winners, do share a few similar traits in their management, not least in their pragmatism, as well as the laissez-faire approach to attacking phases which Deschamps embraced in the recent World Cup.Given the attacking talent at his disposal, it stands to reason that Zidane would carry on in that vein."I was a number 10 as a player," he said, hinting he would retain the role Michael Olise thrived in for much of the summer."What motivates me is the game, it's scoring goals," he added.With the team netting 20 times in North America, Deschamps has arguably laid the foundations for his successor's attacking set-up.Zidane is finding Les Bleus in immeasurably better shape than his predecessor did at the start of his own tenure, at which point the wounds of the 2010 World Cup fiasco were still fresh.The appointment does come with a degree of uncertainty, though.Given that Zidane has spent five years out of management, and the Real Madrid job is the only other senior coaching role of his career, it might seem like a gamble.The 54-year-old himself has acknowledged leading a national team would be an entirely new proposition: "It's new to me, but I'm not scared. This is what I wanted."Predictably, the reaction among players and fans to Zidane's arrival has been almost unanimously positive. He was met with a crowd of supporters carrying flares and banners as he left the French Football Federation's headquarters on Tuesday."Welcome home," Mbappe wrote on Instagram later in the day."It's a great day for French football," his former France and Bordeaux team-mate Bixente Lizarazu told France Info later in the day. "He is more than fit to manage Les Bleus, given what he did at Real Madrid with great players and big egos."The respect that the former Ballon d'Or winner commands in a dressing room is one of his key strengths.Even more so than Deschamps, a France legend in his own right, Zidane is a figure who can rival - perhaps even overshadow - his own players in terms of star power.In this sense, he may be the ideal manager to get the most out of an attack made up of Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele, Desire Doue and Olise.Zidane's four-year deal begins next month, and his full coaching team will be announced a few weeks later.The next international break, lasting four Nations League fixtures over three weeks, will offer the France players a crash-course to the new management style.His first match will involve a trip to Turkey, before two games against Belgium and match against Italy in Paris.Given his iconic status within French football and on the wider national stage, Zidane will invariably enjoy an unprecedented degree of goodwill regardless of his initial results.Whether he uses that leeway to experiment tactically and bring in new faces remains to be seen.His homecoming at the Stade de France in two months' time, against the Azzurri no less, is an ideal fixture to begin the new era.

schema.headline: Zinedine Zidane waited for France - now what will he bring to role?
